why: The array is not sorted, yet 'nums[i] > nums[i + 1]' is false while you climb and true once you descend past the peak, so the peak is the first index where that predicate turns true.
hints: Compare nums[mid] with nums[mid + 1]. If you are going uphill, where must the peak be?
Uphill (nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1]) -> the peak is strictly to the right. Downhill -> the peak is mid or to its left.
lo, hi = 0, n - 1; while lo < hi: if nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1]: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid. Return lo. O(log n).
pitfalls: mid + 1 is always valid because lo < hi.
One element: the loop does not run and index 0 is the peak.
